categories.main_business_segments: China Unicom operates primarily in two main business segments: Connectivity and Communications (CC), which includes mobile connectivity, broadband connectivity, TV connectivity, leased line connectivity, communications service, and information service; and Computing and Digital Smart Applications (CDSA), which includes Unicom Cloud, IDC, system integration, data services, intelligence services, and cybersecurity. The CC segment accounts for approximately 76% of service revenue, while CDSA accounts for about 24%.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages advanced telecommunications technologies including 5G, 5G-A, 10G PON broadband, AI large models, and integrated computing-network infrastructure. It emphasizes network innovation, technology innovation, and service innovation, with significant R&D investment in AI, big data, cloud computing, intelligent computing centers, and next-generation Internet protocols. The company also utilizes co-build co-share network infrastructure and AI empowerment to optimize operations and energy efficiency.
categories.primary_customers_markets: China Unicom serves a broad customer base including individual consumers, government entities, state-owned enterprises, and various industries such as automotive, manufacturing, and digital government services. It supports over 470 million mobile and broadband subscribers, 620 million IoT connections, and 76 million Internet of Vehicles connections. The company also targets industrial Internet applications with over 29,000 5G industrial Internet projects and 7,100 5G factories.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates extensively across Mainland China with branches in 31 provinces and autonomous regions, and has expanded internationally with subsidiaries in countries including Saudi Arabia, Peru, UAE, Uzbekistan, USA, UK, Japan, Singapore, South Africa, Myanmar, Australia, Russia, Brazil, Thailand, Malaysia, Korea, Vietnam, Cambodia, Indonesia, Philippines, Mexico, and others. Its international network covers over 200 countries and regions with over 400 points of presence.
categories.supply_chain_position: China Unicom operates primarily as a downstream telecommunications service provider, offering connectivity and digital services directly to end customers. It also engages in midstream activities such as network infrastructure construction, maintenance, and operation, including joint operations for 5G network infrastructure with China Telecom. Additionally, it provides value-added services, cloud computing, and digital applications, positioning itself as an integrated technology service enterprise.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company’s strategic focus is on integrated innovation encompassing network, technology, and service innovation. It prioritizes AI and big data development, next-generation Internet protocols, 5G-A and 6G research, intelligent computing, and cloud services. R&D investment increased by 9.1% in 2024, with initiatives like the Artificial Intelligence Innovation Center and Data Intelligence Co., Ltd. The company also emphasizes green computing and energy-efficient network infrastructure.
categories.revenue_model: China Unicom generates revenue primarily through telecommunications service fees including voice, broadband, mobile data, and value-added services. It also earns from sales of telecommunications products, cloud computing services, data services, intelligence services, cybersecurity, and international telecommunications services. Revenue streams include subscription fees, usage charges, interconnection fees, and project-based contracts for industrial Internet and digital smart applications.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: China Unicom is one of the leading telecommunications operators in China, ranked 279th in the 2024 Fortune Global 500 and recognized as Asia’s Most Honored Telecom Company for nine consecutive years. It competes with other major Chinese telecom operators such as China Mobile and China Telecom. The company positions itself as a pioneer in digital technology integration and innovation with a strong focus on AI and cloud computing to differentiate from competitors.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2024, China Unicom reported operating revenue of RMB 389.6 billion, a 4.6% increase year-on-year, with net profit attributable to equity shareholders rising 10.1% to RMB 20.6 billion. The company’s service revenue grew steadily, with the CDSA segment growing faster at 9.6%. Capital expenditure was RMB 61.37 billion, down 17%, while R&D expenses increased by 9.1%. The company maintains a strong balance sheet with total assets of RMB 671.2 billion and a liabilities-to-assets ratio of 45.8%.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: China Unicom emphasizes integrated digital services that combine connectivity, cloud computing, AI, and big data to empower industries and consumers. Its value proposition includes comprehensive network coverage, advanced 5G and intelligent computing infrastructure, and innovative AI large models tailored for industry-specific applications. The company focuses on high-quality service, green and energy-efficient operations, and a one-stop cloudified digital platform to enhance customer satisfaction and drive digital transformation.
